transcript.text: my belling cooker keeps burnin stuff 1 day then next day its undercookd on same temp. been like it a cuple months. thermastat??

Quite possibly. An oven that burns one day and undercooks the next at the same setting is a classic sign of a failing thermostat, but whether that's the culprit depends partly on what type of temperature control your Belling has. From what you have described, the most likely cause is mechanical oven thermostat [dial/capillary ovens]. Is it a dial-thermostat oven or an electronic one with a digital temperature display?
its got knobs, mechanical i think, with a little orange light thats the neon i think. no digital display or anything. i do alot of baking and roasts so its a nuisance
Is it running much too hot (burning even on low), or does it go cold after a while - and does it trip the electrics when it does?

its not burnin on low as far as i know, just on 180 mostly, then other days like my lasagne was still cold in the middle after the usual time. no tripping or burnin smell, nothing like that. its only the main fan oven, the top oven and grill are fine
Next: Check whether the temperature is far above the setting and whether it ever cycles off. Let me know what you find.
i dont have an oven thermometer so cant tell how hot it really gets. the orange light goes off after about 10 mins sometimes, other times it seems to stay on for ages. is that what you meant?

If you mean watching the orange light, yes, that's what I meant, and noting that it sometimes goes off after about 10 minutes but other times stays on for ages is exactly the useful detail. Without an oven thermometer we can't know the actual temperature, so the next step is to see how a normal bake turns out. Try a normal bake at the right temperature and keep an eye on it. Is it cooking at a normal temperature now, or still too hot?
i dont know if its too hot now, no thermometer so cant tell. its just been up and down for months really. what should i do next?

First the simple things: check the temperature knob or display matches what you want, the function isn't on grill or a "fast heat / booster" mode, and that recipes for a fan oven are usually 10–20°C lower than conventional. Was a setting or function wrong (and have you changed it), or was it all set normally?
its all set normal as far as i know, same as always and i havent changed my recipes. the knob is a bit wobbly tho, not sure if thats relevant

It could be. If the knob is loose on the thermostat shaft, it may not be setting the temperature the dial shows, which would fit the up-and-down results. Could you tell me a bit more about what it is doing, and when it happens?

well it happens on and off, no real pattern by day that ive noticed. sometimes i put stuff in straight away without preheating all the way, not sure if that matters. i dont know the model number either, cant find the label

It can make a difference, as food put in early cooks more slowly and could leave something like a lasagne cold in the middle. But it wouldn't explain food burning at the same setting on other days, so it's unlikely to be the whole story. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
